Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)
Referred Sections: CMM-609.8: Repeat Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) at the Same Level

Required findings: Greater than six (6) months elapsed since the index lumbar fusion procedure
Daily pain of clinically significant intensity causing functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, inability to stand for prolonged periods)
Physical examination findings that are concordant with the reported pain and level of pseudoarthrosis

Failure to achieve clinically meaningful improvement despite BOTH (a) prescription‑strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs for a minimum of six (6) weeks AND (b) a provider‑directed exercise/physical therapy program for a minimum of six (6) weeks
Post‑operative imaging performed at least six (6) months after the prior fusion that demonstrates pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s) (plain radiographs, CT, or dynamic flexion‑extension views)
MRI or CT study that correlates the imaging findings with the patient’s symptoms
No unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorder (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, opioid use disorder, secondary gain)
Documented nicotine‑free status either as a never‑smoker or abstinence for ≥ six (6) weeks verified by objective cotinine testing (serum, urine, or saliva)
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.8: Repeat Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) at the Same Level > Symptomatic Pseudoarthrosis

Non-Indications: Interval of less than six (6) months since the prior lumbar fusion
Absence of imaging evidence of pseudoarthrosis at the symptomatic level
Pain that is mild, intermittent, or does not produce functional limitation
Demonstrated clinically meaningful improvement with either pharmacologic therapy or a structured exercise program
Unmanaged or uncontrolled significant mental/behavioral health disorder
Active tobacco use without documented cessation or without a normal cotinine test result
Failure to complete the required six‑week trial of both pharmacologic and exercise conservative therapy
Imaging that shows stable fusion without pseudoarthrosis
Important criteria & exceptions: All listed criteria must be satisfied; omission of any single element renders the request non‑medically necessary
Objective cotinine testing may be serum, urinary, or salivary; the result must be within the normal range for the assay used
Behavioral health disorders must be addressed and documented as stable or managed before surgery
Imaging to confirm pseudoarthrosis must be performed no earlier than six (6) months post‑operative to avoid false‑positive motion artifacts
Documentation required: Operative report of the index lumbar fusion (including levels fused and date of surgery)
Post‑operative plain radiographs (including flexion‑extension views) or CT performed ≥6 months after the index surgery showing pseudoarthrosis
MRI or CT report demonstrating pseudoarthrosis and correlating neural element compression or instability
Detailed clinical notes describing daily pain intensity, functional limitations, and concordant physical exam findings
Medication administration record or prescription history confirming ≥6 weeks of prescription‑strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs
Physical therapy or structured exercise program notes confirming ≥6 weeks of supervised therapy directed by a qualified provider
Behavioral health evaluation note confirming absence of unmanaged significant mental or substance‑use disorder
Smoking cessation documentation and objective cotinine test result (serum, urine, or saliva) within normal limits
